The owner-signed head is the authority; compaction must be\n39\t    owner-key-gated.\n40\t12. **read-path presents ONE contiguous genesis chain** — entries()/iter_records(-1)/verify()/count()\n41\t    must transparently concatenate snapshot-front + sealed segments + active segment in seq order, no\n42\t    gap/dup at a seam, so all 34 consumers keep working unchanged.\n43\t13. **durable tip determines next_seq (no seq reuse)** — `_read_last_entry`/next_seq must resolve the tip\n44\t    from the ACTIVE segment (true global max seq).\n45\t14. **cross-writer serialization must cover the compactor** — spine_lock (RLock) + flock. Serializes `append` (read-tip → write)\n57\t    across threads so concurrent writers can't fork the hash chain, and — being re-entrant — lets a\n58\t    caller make a check-then-append atomic (e.g. the nonce replay gate) while its inner `append` still\n59\t    acquires the same lock. Cross-PROCESS serialization is added by an flock inside `append`.\"\"\"\n60\t    key = str(Path(path).resolve())\n61\t    with _LOCKS_GUARD:\n62\t        lk = _LOCKS.get(key)\n63\t        if lk is None:\n64\t            lk = _LOCKS[key] = threading.RLock()\n65\t        return lk\n66\t\n67\t\n68\tdef _last_nonempty_line(path: Path) -> str | None:\n69\t    \"\"\"Read the last VALID record line without loading the file (seek-from-end). A torn/garbage tail\n70\t    line — a partial write from a crash — is SKIPPED so a read/restart never blows up on it: we return\n71\t    the last line that JSON-parses and carries the chain fields (FIX 2). None if no valid line exists.\n72\t    For a clean file this returns exactly the last non-empty line, byte-for-byte as before.\"\"\"\n73\t    try:\n74\t        size = path.stat().st_size\n75\t    except OSError:\n76\t        return None\n77\t    if size == 0:\n78\t        return None\n79\t    window = 8192\n80\t    while True:\n81\t        start = max(0, size - window)\n82\t        with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n83\t            f.seek(start)\n84\t            buf = f.read(size - start)\n85\t        lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n86\t        if start > 0 and lines:\n87\t            lines = lines[1:]                       # the first line may be partial unless we are at BOF\n88\t        for raw in reversed(lines):\n89\t            try:\n90\t                d = json.loads(raw)\n91\t            except ValueError:\n92\t                d = None\n93\t            if isinstance(d, dict) and all(k in d for k in _REQUIRED_KEYS):\n94\t                return raw.decode(\"utf-8\")\n95\t            _log.warning(\"spine: skipping malformed tail line while seeking the tip (%s)\", path)\n96\t        if start == 0:\n97\t            return None                             # scanned the whole file, no valid line\n98\t        window *= 4                                 # a torn tail bigger than the window (rare) — widen\n99\t\n100\t\n101\tdef _last_valid_boundary(path: Path) -> \"tuple[int, ChainEntry | None]\":\n102\t    \"\"\"Return (byte offset just past the last VALID record line, its ChainEntry) — bytes BEYOND that\n103\t    offset are a torn tail from an interrupted write, which `append` truncates before writing so the new\n104\t    record cannot merge with them and be silently lost (BLOCK-1). (0, None) for an empty / all-torn file.\n105\t    For a clean file the offset equals the file size (nothing to truncate).\"\"\"\n106\t    try:\n107\t        size = path.stat().st_size\n108\t    except OSError:\n109\t        return 0, None\n110\t    if size == 0:\n111\t        return 0, None\n112\t    window = 8192\n113\t    while True:\n114\t        start = max(0, size - window)\n115\t        with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n116\t            f.seek(start)\n117\t            buf = f.read(size - start)\n118\t        segs: list[tuple[int, bytes]] = []          # (byte offset just past this line's \\n, line bytes)\n119\t        i = 0\n120\t        while True:\n121\t            nl = buf.find(b\"\\n\", i)\n122\t            if nl == -1:\n123\t                break\n124\t            segs.append((start + nl + 1, buf[i:nl]))\n125\t            i = nl + 1\n126\t        for end, raw in reversed(segs):             # near-EOF first; front partials (start>0) never win\n127\t            if not raw.strip():\n128\t                continue\n129\t            try:\n130\t                d = json.loads(raw)\n131\t            except ValueError:\n132\t                d = None\n133\t            if isinstance(d, dict) and all(k in d for k in _REQUIRED_KEYS):\n134\t                return end, ChainEntry(seq=d[\"seq\"], prev_hash=d[\"prev_hash\"],\n135\t                                       cert_digest=d[\"cert_digest\"], entry_hash=d[\"entry_hash\"])\n136\t            _log.warning(\"spine: skipping malformed tail segment while seeking the tip (%s)\", path)\n137\t        if start == 0:\n138\t            return 0, None\n139\t        window *= 4\n140\t\n141\t\n142\tclass SpineStore:\n143\t    def __init__(self, path: Path | str = SPINE_PATH) -> None:\n144\t        # `self.path` is the STABLE identity + lock token (…/spine.jsonl). After a migration it is renamed\n145\t        # away and no longer a data file, but it remains the key for the in-process RLock and the anchor\n146\t        # the whole layout derives from — so the RLock that `envelope.consume` shares with `append` stays\n147\t        # the same object across a rotation (invariant 14). All DATA I/O targets `self._active` (the\n148\t        # manifest's active segment, or — with no manifest yet — the legacy single file in place, which is\n149\t        # byte-identical to the pre-rotation store).\n150\t        self.path = Path(path)\n151\t        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n152\t        self._layout = SpineLayout.for_path(self.path)\n153\t        # NB: `segments/` is created only when actually migrating/rotating (not on every construction), so a\n154\t        # legacy/fresh store leaves the spine dir byte-identical to today (no stray empty dirs).\n155\t        self._manifest: Manifest | None = read_manifest(self._layout)\n156\t        self._reconcile_orphan_migration()          # complete a migrate() interrupted before the manifest write\n157\t        self._active: Path = self._resolve_active_path()\n158\t        # SEGMENT-AWARE seq -> (segment file, byte offset) index (Slice 1). Sealed segments are immutable,\n159\t        # so each is indexed once and its offsets kept forever; the active segment's tail extends on our own\n160\t        # appends (O(1)) or on the next read (over just the newly-appended bytes — offsets never move). Full\n161\t        # scans (verify/count/entries/iter_records(-1)) never touch the index, staying a single pass across\n162\t        # segments. Invalidation is EPOCH-based (`change_token`: manifest generation + active dev/ino/size),\n163\t        # so a rotation/migration is detected — a same-size in-place rewrite can no longer fool a size-only\n164\t        # heuristic (invariant 9). `_index_lock` guards the dicts against concurrent read+append.\n165\t        self._index_lock = threading.Lock()\n166\t        self._offsets: dict[int, tuple[str, int]] = {}   # seq -> (segment path str, byte offset in it)\n167\t        self._seg_scanned: dict[str, int] = {}           # segment path str -> bytes indexed so far\n168\t        self._index_epoch: tuple | None = None           # change_token when the index was last reconciled\n169\t        self._max_seq = -1\n170\t        self._last: ChainEntry | None = self._read_last_entry()\n171\t\n172\t    # --- segment layout / manifest ------------------------------------------------\n173\t    def _resolve_active_path(self) -> Path:\n174\t        \"\"\"The current append/read target. With a manifest, the active segment's absolute path; without\n175\t        one (a fresh or not-yet-migrated legacy spine), the legacy single file in place — byte-identical\n176\t        to the pre-rotation store, so nothing destructive happens until an explicit `migrate()`. A manifest\n177\t        that exists but names NO active segment is a corrupt/degenerate state and RAISES rather than\n178\t        silently falling back to `spine.jsonl` (which would resurrect a data file OUTSIDE the segment set —\n179\t        a fork; the guard also removes the same landmine for Slice-3 sealing, which must always leave an\n180\t        active segment).\"\"\"\n181\t        if self._manifest is not None:\n182\t            act = self._manifest.active()\n183\t            if act is None:\n184\t                raise SpineError(\"manifest has no active segment (corrupt/degenerate) — refusing to \"\n185\t                                 \"resurrect spine.jsonl outside the segment set\")\n186\t            return self._layout.seg_path(act)\n187\t        return self.path\n188\t\n189\t    def _read_target(self) -> Path:\n190\t        \"\"\"The file to read for THIS operation. Normally the cached active segment; if it has VANISHED (a\n191\t        migrate()/rotation in another process renamed it away), resolve the current active from the\n192\t        manifest for this read only — WITHOUT mutating shared state (lock-free reads must not race\n193\t        append's active update). Prevents a false-EMPTY read during the migrate instant, which for the\n194\t        nonce-highwater scan would regress the replay floor. In Slice 0 the only mover is migrate(), which\n195\t        RENAMES (byte-preserving), so the current index offsets stay valid for the resolved file. Fully\n196\t        epoch-invalidated, segment-spanning reads land in Slice 1.\"\"\"\n197\t        a = self._active\n198\t        if a.exists():\n199\t            return a\n200\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n201\t        act = m.active() if m is not None else None\n202\t        if act is not None:\n203\t            r = self._layout.seg_path(act)\n204\t            if r.exists():\n205\t                return r\n206\t        # PRE-manifest migrate window: the atomic rename has already placed the data at seg-0 but the\n207\t        # manifest is not published yet (so `m is None`). Read it there — otherwise a lock-free reader in\n208\t        # exactly this instant sees a false-EMPTY spine (kill-switch un-halt / nonce-floor regression) and\n209\t        # the indexed read path can hit a bare FileNotFoundError. seg-0 is byte-identical (rename), so the\n210\t        # index built over the vanished file stays valid on it.\n211\t        if m is None:\n212\t            seg0 = self._layout.segments_dir / segment_filename(0)\n213\t            if seg0.exists() and not self.path.exists():\n214\t                return seg0\n215\t        return a\n216\t\n217\t    def _segments_in_order(self) -> list[Path]:\n218\t        \"\"\"The segment files to read, in seq order (sealed by first_seq, then the active tail). With no\n219\t        manifest this is the single legacy/active file. Resolved fresh each call so a rotation/migration by\n220\t        another process is seen. RAISES SpineError on a manifest-referenced segment file that is MISSING —\n221\t        a read must never silently yield a short chain (invariant 15: no state-scanner fail-open).\"\"\"\n222\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n223\t        if m is None:\n224\t            t = self._read_target()\n225\t            return [t] if t.exists() else []\n226\t        out: list[Path] = []\n227\t        for seg in m.ordered():\n228\t            p = self._layout.seg_path(seg)\n229\t            if not p.exists():\n230\t                raise SpineError(\n231\t                    f\"spine manifest (generation {m.generation}) references a missing segment: {seg.file}\")\n232\t            out.append(p)\n233\t        return out\n234\t\n235\t    def _seam_tip_for_active(self) -> \"ChainEntry | None\":\n236\t        \"\"\"When the ACTIVE segment is empty, the chain tip its first append must extend so the seam stays\n237\t        contiguous: the prior SEALED segment's real last record (its boundary). None when the active is the\n238\t        GENESIS segment (first_seq == 0) — a genuinely fresh spine correctly starts at seq 0. Prevents a\n239\t        seq-0 fork across a rotation seam (invariant 13). MUST be consulted under the append lock (reads the\n240\t        manifest fresh). No-op in Slices 0-2 (the only segment is genesis).\"\"\"\n241\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n242\t        if m is None:\n243\t            return None\n244\t        act = m.active()\n245\t        if act is None or act.first_seq == 0:\n246\t            return None\n247\t        sealed = m.sealed_in_order()\n248\t        if not sealed:\n249\t            return None\n250\t        sp = self._layout.seg_path(sealed[-1])\n251\t        line = _last_nonempty_line(sp) if sp.exists() else None\n252\t        if not line:\n253\t            return None\n254\t        d = json.loads(line)\n255\t        return ChainEntry(seq=d[\"seq\"], prev_hash=d[\"prev_hash\"], cert_digest=d[\"cert_digest\"],\n256\t                          entry_hash=d[\"entry_hash\"])\n257\t\n258\t    @contextmanager\n259\t    def _crossproc_lock(self) -> \"Iterator[None]\":\n260\t        \"\"\"Cross-process exclusion on the inode-stable lockfile (invariant 14 / D3). flock binds to the\n261\t        open file DESCRIPTION, not the path, so an os.replace of the manifest/segments cannot move the\n262\t        lock out from under a concurrent writer — which the prior flock-on-the-data-fd could not survive.\n263\t        Best-effort exactly as before (fcntl absent on non-POSIX; a flock failure is swallowed). NOT\n264\t        re-entrant across fds — never nest a second `_crossproc_lock` inside one (a second LOCK_EX on the\n265\t        same file from a different fd self-deadlocks); the seal-swap that runs inside append reuses the\n266\t        already-held lock rather than re-acquiring.\"\"\"\n267\t        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover — non-POSIX\n268\t            yield\n269\t            return\n270\t        self._layout.lockfile_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n271\t        fd = os.open(str(self._layout.lockfile_path), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)\n272\t        try:\n273\t            try:\n274\t                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n275\t            except OSError:  # pragma: no cover\n276\t                pass\n277\t            yield\n278\t        finally:\n279\t            os.close(fd)\n280\t\n281\t    def _complete_orphan_migration_locked(self) -> bool:\n282\t        \"\"\"MUST hold `_crossproc_lock`, and be called only when the manifest is currently ABSENT. If we are\n283\t        in the migrate() crash window — seg-0 present, `spine.jsonl` gone (the rename is atomic + durable),\n284\t        no manifest — finish the interrupted migration by publishing the manifest. Returns True iff it\n285\t        completed one. Called from BOTH __init__'s reconciler AND append's `_refresh_active_under_lock`, so\n286\t        a LIVE appender completes the orphan under the lock instead of re-creating `spine.jsonl` and forking\n287\t        the log (the critical review finding).\"\"\"\n288\t        seg0 = self._layout.segments_dir / segment_filename(0)\n289\t        if seg0.exists() and not self.path.exists():\n290\t            write_manifest(self._layout, initial_manifest(SCOPE, active_file=self._layout.segment_rel(0)))\n291\t            _log.warning(\"spine: completed an interrupted migration — published the manifest for %s\", seg0)\n292\t            return True\n293\t        return False\n294\t\n295\t    def _refresh_active_under_lock(self) -> None:\n296\t        \"\"\"MUST hold `_crossproc_lock`. FIRST complete any interrupted migration (so a live appender never\n297\t        resurrects `spine.jsonl`), THEN re-resolve the active segment from the manifest so an appender\n298\t        constructed before a concurrent migrate()/rotation writes to the CURRENT target — never a stale\n299\t        path (fork) or a renamed-away file (resurrection). One manifest read in the steady state.\"\"\"\n300\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n301\t        if m is None and self._complete_orphan_migration_locked():\n302\t            m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n303\t        new_active = self.path\n304\t        act = m.active() if m is not None else None\n305\t        if act is not None:\n306\t            new_active = self._layout.seg_path(act)\n307\t        if new_active != self._active or (m is not None) != (self._manifest is not None):\n308\t            self._manifest = m\n309\t            self._active = new_active\n310\t            self._invalidate_index()\n311\t            self._last = self._read_last_entry()\n312\t\n313\t    def _invalidate_index(self) -> None:\n314\t        \"\"\"Drops the segment-aware index so the next read rebuilds it against the (possibly changed)\n315\t        segment set.\"\"\"\n316\t        with self._index_lock:\n317\t            self._offsets = {}\n318\t            self._seg_scanned = {}\n319\t            self._index_epoch = None\n320\t            self._max_seq = -1\n321\t\n322\t    def _reconcile_orphan_migration(self) -> None:\n323\t        \"\"\"Close the migrate() crash window at CONSTRUCTION. migrate() does an ATOMIC\n324\t        `os.replace(spine.jsonl → segments/seg-00000000.jsonl)` and THEN publishes the manifest; a crash\n325\t        BETWEEN them leaves seg-0 present, `spine.jsonl` gone, and no manifest — at which point the legacy\n326\t        fallback (active = spine.jsonl) would read the spine as EMPTY and silently hide all history. If we\n327\t        observe exactly that state, finish the (already-durable) migration under the lock. (A live appender\n328\t        does the same via `_refresh_active_under_lock`; a construction-time pass just recovers faster.)\"\"\"\n329\t        if self._manifest is not None:\n330\t            return\n331\t        seg0 = self._layout.segments_dir / segment_filename(0)\n332\t        if not (seg0.exists() and not self.path.exists()):\n333\t            return\n334\t        with self._crossproc_lock():\n335\t            if read_manifest(self._layout) is None:          # re-check under the lock\n336\t                self._complete_orphan_migration_locked()\n337\t            self._manifest = read_manifest(self._layout)\n338\t\n339\t    def change_token(self) -> tuple:\n340\t        \"\"\"A cheap, rotation-aware epoch token — (manifest generation, active file, size, inode) — that\n341\t        changes on ANY append (size), a migration/rotation (generation + active path/inode), or a reset.\n342\t        THE unified replacement for the size-only 'has the spine changed?' heuristic at every site\n343\t        (invariant 9 / A4) — notably the kill-switch verdict caches in `governor/killswitch.py` and\n344\t        `gesture/session.py`. Because it reads the manifest FRESH and keys on the resolved active segment\n345\t        (not the legacy `store.path`, which a migration renames away), a same-size rotation — or a\n346\t        migration performed by another process — can never serve a stale (un-halting) kill-switch verdict.\"\"\"\n347\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n348\t        gen = m.generation if m is not None else -1\n349\t        active = self.path\n350\t        act = m.active() if m is not None else None\n351\t        if act is not None:\n352\t            active = self._layout.seg_path(act)\n353\t        try:\n354\t            st = active.stat()\n355\t            return (gen, str(active), st.st_size, st.st_ino)\n356\t        except OSError:\n357\t            return (gen, str(active), -1, -1)\n358\t\n359\t    def migrate(self) -> bool:\n360\t        \"\"\"Move a legacy single-file spine into the segment layout: rename `spine.jsonl` →\n361\t        `<stem>.segments/seg-00000000.jsonl` (atomic, same filesystem — O(1), no byte copy) and publish a\n362\t        single-active-segment manifest. Idempotent (a no-op once a manifest exists). Returns True iff it\n363\t        migrated. SPLIT-BRAIN SAFETY: run this only after every spine writer is on code that flocks the\n364\t        path-stable lockfile (this Slice-0 code) and re-resolves the active segment under that lock — a\n365\t        stale appender then completes/observes the migration instead of resurrecting `spine.jsonl`. After\n366\t        migration `spine.jsonl` is absent and is NEVER re-created as a data file (all data I/O targets the\n367\t        active segment).\"\"\"\n368\t        with spine_lock(self.path):\n369\t            with self._crossproc_lock():\n370\t                if read_manifest(self._layout) is not None:\n371\t                    self._refresh_active_under_lock()\n372\t                    return False\n373\t                self._layout.segments_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n374\t                seg0_abs = self._layout.segments_dir / segment_filename(0)\n375\t                if self.path.exists():\n376\t                    os.replace(self.path, seg0_abs)         # atomic rename (same fs); O(1), no copy\n377\t                    fsync_dir(self._layout.spine_dir)       # persist the SOURCE-dir unlink of spine.jsonl\n378\t                else:\n379\t                    seg0_abs.touch()                        # fresh spine: create the empty active segment\n380\t                fsync_dir(self._layout.segments_dir)        # persist the TARGET-dir creation of seg-0\n381\t                write_manifest(self._layout, initial_manifest(SCOPE, active_file=self._layout.segment_rel(0)))\n382\t                self._manifest = read_manifest(self._layout)\n383\t                self._active = self._resolve_active_path()\n384\t                self._invalidate_index()\n385\t                self._last = self._read_last_entry()\n386\t                return True\n387\t\n388\t    def reset(self) -> None:\n389\t        \"\"\"Delete EVERY spine artifact for this store — the legacy data file, the manifest, all segments,\n390\t        the trash, and the lockfile — for `sigil ingest --reset` (a full rebuild). Under the cross-process\n391\t        lock so it can't race an append. Idempotent; leaves the store readable (empty) afterward. Replaces\n392\t        the old `SPINE_PATH.unlink()`, which left the manifest + rotated segments behind (stale).\"\"\"\n393\t        with spine_lock(self.path):\n394\t            with self._crossproc_lock():\n395\t                for pth in (self._layout.manifest_path, self.path, self._layout.lockfile_path):\n396\t                    try:\n397\t                        pth.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n398\t                    except OSError:\n399\t                        pass\n400\t                for dpath in (self._layout.segments_dir, self._layout.trash_dir):\n401\t                    if dpath.exists():\n402\t                        shutil.rmtree(dpath, ignore_errors=True)\n403\t                self._manifest = None\n404\t                self._active = self._resolve_active_path()\n405\t                self._invalidate_index()\n406\t                self._last = self._read_last_entry()\n407\t\n408\t    def generation(self) -> int:\n409\t        \"\"\"The manifest generation (monotonic rotation epoch); -1 for a legacy (un-migrated) spine.\"\"\"\n410\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n411\t        return m.generation if m is not None else -1\n412\t\n413\t    def segment_info(self) -> list[dict]:\n414\t        \"\"\"A CLI/human summary of the segment set: one dict per segment in seq order. Empty list for a\n415\t        legacy (un-migrated) single-file spine.\"\"\"\n416\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n417\t        if m is None:\n418\t            return []\n419\t        out: list[dict] = []\n420\t        for seg in m.ordered():\n421\t            p = self._layout.seg_path(seg)\n422\t            out.append({\"id\": seg.id, \"codec\": seg.codec, \"sealed\": seg.sealed,\n423\t                        \"first_seq\": seg.first_seq, \"last_seq\": seg.last_seq,\n424\t                        \"bytes\": p.stat().st_size if p.exists() else 0, \"file\": seg.file})\n425\t        return out\n426\t\n427\t    # --- write --------------------------------------------------------------------\n428\t    def append(\n429\t        self, *, kind: str, source: str, actor: str, payload: dict[str, Any],\n430\t        parent_id: int | None = None, supersedes_id: int | None = None,\n431\t        ts: str | None = None,\n432\t    ) -> int:\n433\t        content = {\n434\t            \"scope\": SCOPE, \"kind\": kind, \"source\": source, \"actor\": actor,\n435\t            \"payload\": payload, \"parent_id\": parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": supersedes_id,\n436\t        }\n437\t        cert_digest = digest_payload(content)  # wallclock-free\n438\t        # Serialize the whole read-tip → write so concurrent writers (threaded bridge server, gesture\n439\t        # daemon) can't both fork off a stale tip and break the chain. The in-process RLock is keyed on\n440\t        # the STABLE `self.path` (unchanged), so the check-then-append gate `envelope.consume` builds on\n441\t        # top of it stays atomic across a rotation. Re-read the TRUE tip from disk under the lock.\n442\t        with spine_lock(self.path):\n443\t            with self._crossproc_lock():                 # cross-process guard on the path-stable lockfile\n444\t                self._refresh_active_under_lock()        # pick up a concurrent migrate()/rotation; never fork\n445\t                active = self._active\n446\t                # binary append+read: lets us TRUNCATE a torn tail before writing (BLOCK-1 fix). `a+b`\n447\t                # creates the file if absent and — in append mode — every write still lands at EOF.\n448\t                with active.open(\"a+b\") as f:\n449\t                    # BLOCK-1: an interrupted write can leave torn bytes PAST the last valid record. Appending\n450\t                    # after them would MERGE (torn + new) into one unparseable line → the new record is silently\n451\t                    # lost, verify() stays green, and a lost kill-switch panic never halts the mesh. Truncate the\n452\t                    # dead tail back to the last valid record FIRST (this only removes never-committed garbage\n453\t                    # from an interrupted write; committed records are untouched). Evaluated on the ACTIVE\n454\t                    # segment under the lock (invariant 7 — the append target is always the true chain tip).\n455\t                    clean_end, last = _last_valid_boundary(active)\n456\t                    pre_size = os.fstat(f.fileno()).st_size\n457\t                    if pre_size > clean_end:\n458\t                        f.truncate(clean_end)\n459\t                        _log.warning(\"spine: truncated a %d-byte torn tail (interrupted write) before append (%s)\",\n460\t                                     pre_size - clean_end, active)\n461\t                    if last is not None:\n462\t                        entry = append_entry([last], cert_digest)          # extend the active segment's tip\n463\t                    else:\n464\t                        # active is EMPTY: seed from the prior sealed segment's boundary if this is a rotated\n465\t                        # (non-genesis) segment, else start the genesis chain at seq 0. It is deliberately UNSIGNED and\n5\tNON-LOAD-BEARING: record order, count, and every tamper decision are re-derived from the segment BYTES\n6\t(via `verify_chain`/`classify_head`), never from the manifest's convenience fields. A doctored manifest\n7\ttherefore fails CLOSED — dropping/reordering an interior segment breaks `prev_hash`/seq contiguity, a\n8\tdropped tail shortens `entries()` (the signed head's `n < entry_count` gate fires), a dropped front fails\n9\tthe genesis check. (A future signed-manifest tier would set `manifest_sig` — reserved `null` — because it\n10\twould then attest pruned ranges; retain-all needs no such trust.)\n11\t\n12\t`SpineLayout` derives the whole on-disk layout from the spine data-file path a `SpineStore` is constructed\n13\twith, so a store on a temp path is fully isolated. This module does no locking — the caller (`SpineStore`)\n14\tholds the cross-process flock while reading/writing/migrating.\n15\t\"\"\"\n16\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n17\t\n18\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n19\tfrom pathlib import PurePosixPath, Path\n20\t\n21\tfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator\n22\t\n23\tfrom ..reuse.chain import _GENESIS_PREV\n24\tfrom .atomicio import atomic_write_text\n25\t\n26\tSEGMENT_STEM = \"seg-\"\n27\t_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n28\t\n29\t\n30\tdef segment_filename(seg_id: int, codec: str = \"none\") -> str:\n31\t    \"\"\"Zero-padded segment file name; `.gz` suffix when gzip-sealed (Slice 4).\"\"\"\n32\t    base = f\"{SEGMENT_STEM}{seg_id:08d}.jsonl\"\n33\t    return base + \".gz\" if codec == \"gzip\" else base\n34\t\n35\t\n36\tclass Segment(BaseModel):\n37\t    \"\"\"One segment in the manifest. `first_prev_hash`/`boundary_hash` are the chain-linkage the reader\n38\t    CROSS-CHECKS against the segment's real first/last records — they are convenience, not authority.\"\"\"\n39\t    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"ignore\")   # forward-compatible: tolerate fields a newer writer added\n40\t    id: int = Field(ge=0)\n41\t    file: str                                    # path RELATIVE to the spine dir, e.g. \"segments/seg-00000000.jsonl\"\n42\t    codec: str = \"none\"                          # \"none\" | \"gzip\"\n43\t    sealed: bool = False\n44\t    first_seq: int = Field(ge=0)\n45\t    last_seq: int | None = None                  # null while active\n46\t    count: int | None = None                     # null while active; CONVENIENCE ONLY — never a tamper input\n47\t    first_prev_hash: str = _GENESIS_PREV         # == the prior segment's boundary_hash (seg 0 == genesis)\n48\t    boundary_hash: str | None = None             # == entry_hash(last_seq); null while active\n49\t    bytes: int = 0\n50\t    sha256: str | None = None                    # at-rest file integrity; NOT a chain digest\n51\t\n52\t    @field_validator(\"file\")\n53\t    @classmethod\n54\t    def _file_is_contained_relative(cls, v: str) -> str:\n55\t        \"\"\"A segment `file` must be a plain relative path under the spine dir — never absolute and never\n56\t        `..`-escaping. `get()`/`iter_records()`/`tail()` open segment files WITHOUT running verify(), so a\n57\t        doctored manifest pointing `file` at `/etc/passwd` or `../../secret` would otherwise surface that\n58\t        file's bytes AS spine records. Reject it at the model boundary so the read path stays fail-closed\n59\t        even though the manifest itself is unsigned.\"\"\"\n60\t        pp = PurePosixPath(v)\n61\t        if not v or pp.is_absolute() or PurePosixPath(v.replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")).is_absolute() or \"..\" in pp.parts:\n62\t            raise ValueError(f\"segment file must be a contained relative path, got {v!r}\")\n63\t        return v\n64\t\n65\t\n66\tclass Manifest(BaseModel):\n67\t    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"ignore\")\n68\t    schema_version: int = _SCHEMA_VERSION\n69\t    generation: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)     # monotonic epoch; ++ on EVERY swap — the unified change token\n70\t    scope: str = \"\"\n71\t    segments: list[Segment] = Field(default_factory=list)\n72\t    manifest_sig: str | None = None              # reserved for the deferred signed-manifest tier\n73\t\n74\t    def active(self) -> Segment | None:\n75\t        \"\"\"The single unsealed (append) segment, if any. The contract:\na reader observes either the whole old file or the whole new file (never a torn one), and the new\ncontent survives a crash at any point — a crash mid-write leaves the PREVIOUS valid file intact.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef fsync_dir(directory: Path | str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"fsync a directory so a rename/create inside it is itself durable across a crash. A no-op-on-error\n    on filesystems that don't support directory fsync (the rename still lands; only its durability window\n    widens).\"\"\"\n    try:\n        dfd = os.open(str(directory), os.O_DIRECTORY)\n        try:\n            os.fsync(dfd)\n        finally:\n            os.close(dfd)\n    except OSError:  # pragma: no cover — dir fsync unsupported on some filesystems\n        pass\n\n\ndef atomic_write_text(path: Path | str, data: str, *, prefix: str = \".tmp-\") -> None:\n    \"\"\"Durably + atomically replace `path` with `data`: write a temp file in the SAME dir, fsync it,\n    `os.replace()` over the target (atomic on POSIX), then fsync the directory so the rename survives a\n    crash. A crash at any point leaves the previous valid file intact, never a partially-written one.\"\"\"\n    path = Path(path)\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=prefix, suffix=\".tmp\")\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n            f.write(data)\n            f.flush()\n            os.fsync(f.fileno())\n        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    except BaseException:\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp)\n        except OSError:\n            pass\n        raise\n    fsync_dir(path.parent)","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"e0fb3196-fe53-4e40-bc59-9886ce6681a9","timestamp":"2026-07-19T17:48:19.347Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0b5055c3-46cf-4b0b-8d73-f2f556bb04f7","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Baseline suite is green (17/17) before and the findings survive it — the tests never exercise these interleavings.\n\n---\n\n## FINDING 1 — BLOCK (reachable today): `reset()` unlinks the very lockfile it holds → cross-process exclusion is defeated → a concurrent append is lost AND the store is bricked\n`sigil/spine/store.py:388-406` (`reset`), interacting with `_crossproc_lock` at `:258-279`.\n\n`reset()` runs under `_crossproc_lock`, which `os.open(...O_CREAT)` + `flock`s `spine.lock`. Then reset's first loop (`:395`) unlinks `self._layout.lockfile_path` **while still holding the flock on that fd**, and only afterward `rmtree`s `segments/` and `trash/` (`:400-402`). flock binds to the inode, not the path (this is the framework's own invariant 14). So during the destructive `rmtree` window, a concurrent appender in **another process** calls `_crossproc_lock`, `os.open` **creates a brand-new inode at the same path**, and its `flock` succeeds immediately — it is not excluded by reset at all.\n\nMechanism, isolated:\n```\nH: acquired flock on inode 482205\nH: unlinked the lockfile path (still holding flock on the old inode); now doing rmtree...\nC: opened lockfile, inode 482206\nC: *** ACQUIRED flock while reset() still holds it -> MUTUAL EXCLUSION DEFEATED ***\nCONTROL (no unlink): C correctly BLOCKED\n```\n\nEnd-to-end, with a **real second process** appending during reset of a migrated single-segment spine (exactly what ships in slices 1-2; `sigil ingest --reset` → `SpineStore().reset()` at `cli.py:22`, while the bridge/gesture/governor daemons append to the same default spine):\n```\nsetup: migrated spine with 3 records\n   (concurrent process ran DURING reset:) APPENDER: got ack for seq 3 -> caller believes it's durable\n      \"spine: completed an interrupted migration — published the manifest ...\"\nAFTER reset: SpineError: manifest (generation 0) references a missing segment: spine.segments/seg-00000000.jsonl\n```\nConsequence chain: reset unlinks the manifest (loop 1) → the admitted appender's constructor sees the orphan-migration state (`spine.jsonl` gone, seg-0 present, no manifest) and **re-publishes the manifest**, then appends seq 3 and **returns an ack** → reset's loop-2 `rmtree` then deletes `segments/`. Net result: the acked seq-3 record is **lost**, and the re-published manifest now dangles at a deleted segment, so **every subsequent read (`iter_records`/`count`/`verify`/`entries`) raises `SpineError` permanently** — the store is bricked, not \"readable (empty) afterward\" as the docstring promises. Fix direction: never unlink the path-stable lockfile in `reset()` (leave it; it's tiny and its whole purpose is path-stability), or drain/refuse behind a real barrier.\n\n## FINDING 2 — fix before Slice 3: `get()` fails **open** on a missing referenced segment while every scan fails closed (contradicts its own \"byte-identical to a full scan\" contract)\n`sigil/spine/store.py:531-556` (`get`), `_ensure_index` swallow at `:689-692`.\n\n`_ensure_index` has `except SpineError: return` — on a manifest-referenced segment that is missing it silently returns, leaving a **warm index** (built while the spine was whole) in place. `get(seq)` then hits `_offsets` (`:539-548`) and returns the record straight from a **surviving** segment, never re-checking that a *different* referenced segment has vanished. Meanwhile `_segments_in_order()` (`:229-231`) makes `iter_records`/`count`/`verify`/`entries` all raise. Reproduced on a 3-segment spine after deleting sealed seg-0 (seq 0-2):\n```\n  iter_records / count / verify / entries: raised SpineError (fail closed, good)\n  get(5) with seg-0 MISSING -> {'n': 5}     # returns a value...\n  get(8) with seg-0 MISSING -> {'n': 8}     # ...while the chain is provably broken\n  get(1) [in the missing segment]           -> raises SpineError\n```\nSo `get()` of a seq in a surviving segment silently succeeds while the log is provably truncated — a fail-open point read that violates invariant 15's spirit and the method's own docstring (\"byte-identical to a full scan\"; a full scan raises).
